title: Custodian detection mechanics for the Documenter CHANGELOG fix
question: Custodian detection mechanics for the Documenter CHANGELOG fix: the Documenter needs to distinguish the version-bump custodian task from siblings to suppress its own CHANGELOG.md edit. Option A is DoD-grep — the Documenter reads the Plan JSON, loads each sibling task, and pattern-matches definition_of_done entries for 'package.json version bump' or '## <version> CHANGELOG' strings; this requires no schema change but is fragile against DoD phrasing variation. Option B is an explicit annotation — the Plan agent emits extensions.clv.version-bump-custodian: true on the custodian task during breakdown; the Documenter reads the extensions field directly. The task schema's extensions field already supports namespaced keys without Standard modification, making Option B viable today. A spike should confirm the extensions-based approach (validate that cloverleaf-cli loadTask exposes the extensions field to the Documenter) and draft the exact Documenter prompt fragment for the chosen path.
findings: Confirmed Option B is fully viable. (1) task.schema.json line 73 declares 'extensions' as an explicit optional property referencing extensions.schema.json — it is schema-defined, not an additionalProperty, so tasks carrying 'extensions: {"clv.version-bump-custodian": true}' or 'extensions: {"clv.changelog-suppressed": true}' pass AJV validation today with zero Standard changes. (2) extensions.schema.json patternProperties regex '^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*\.[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$' matches both 'clv.version-bump-custodian' and 'clv.changelog-suppressed'. (3) task.ts loadTask is a raw JSON.parse cast to TaskDoc (which has a [key: string]: unknown index signature) — extensions round-trips intact through read/write with no stripping. (4) plan.ts materialiseTasksFromPlan pre-validates each task via AJV then writes with JSON.stringify — extensions survive materialization. (5) cloverleaf-document/SKILL.md step 5 substitutes {{task}} with 'full task JSON (pretty-printed)' sourced from cloverleaf-cli load-task, which calls loadTask — so extensions ARE present in the Documenter's {{task}} input. Critical gap: the Documenter receives only its own task JSON (no Plan context, no sibling visibility). A flag set on the custodian task (clv.version-bump-custodian: true) is therefore invisible to sibling Documenters. The fix requires the Plan agent to also mark each non-custodian sibling task with extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"]: true at breakdown time. plan.md currently has no concept of extensions; a ~4-line addition suffices and the 'emit ONLY schema-defined fields' constraint is not violated (extensions is schema-defined). Immediate dogfood path confirmed: a human can hand-write extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"]: true on non-custodian tasks in the v0.6.2 Plan JSON today — schema validates it with zero Standard or reference-impl code changes needed.
recommendation: Adopt Option B with a dual-flag variant. Plan agent emits extensions["clv.version-bump-custodian"]: true on the custodian task and extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"]: true on each non-custodian sibling at breakdown time; plan.md needs a ~4-line addition to instruct this. Documenter prompt (documenter.md) gains a ~6-line preflight block before any CHANGELOG.md edit: 'If task.extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"] === true, return {"commits_added": 0, "files_changed": [], "summary": "CHANGELOG suppressed: custodian sibling handles version bump and release section."} immediately without touching CHANGELOG.md. If task.extensions["clv.version-bump-custodian"] === true, proceed with the CHANGELOG write as directed by this task's definition_of_done (typically writing the ## <version> release section rather than ## [Unreleased]).' Both changes are prompt-only, v0.6.2-sized, and require no schema or code modifications. Immediate dogfood path: hand-set extensions["clv.changelog-suppressed"]: true on non-custodian tasks in the v0.6.2 Plan JSON right now — no tooling change required.
